# package client

```go
import "github.com/otfabric/go-iec60870-5/iec103/client"
```

Package client is the controlling system of IEC 60870-5-103: the primary station of unbalanced transmission (clause 6.2.3) that polls one item of protection equipment, runs the application functions of clause 7.4 (station initialization, time synchronization, general interrogation, general commands, generic services, disturbance data transfer) and delivers every monitor-direction ASDU to a handler.

The link is initialized in the background (request status of link, then reset CU or reset FCB, clause 7.4.1) and again when the protection equipment stops answering; [Client.WaitUp](#func-client-waitup) waits for it. Requests fail with [iec103.ErrLinkDown](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-iec60870-5/iec103#ErrLinkDown) while the link is down.

One client serves one item of protection equipment on a transport of its own; one primary polling several items on a shared line is not supported yet.

#### func (Client) BeginWrite

```go
func (c *Client) BeginWrite() (*StagedWrite, error)
```

BeginWrite starts a staged generic write with a new RII. It returns [iec103.ErrBusy](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-iec60870-5/iec103#ErrBusy) while another generic write runs. The caller must end it with [StagedWrite.Execute](#func-stagedwrite-execute) or [StagedWrite.Abort](#func-stagedwrite-abort).

#### func (Client) Broadcast

```go
func (c *Client) Broadcast(a *iec103.ASDU) error
```

Broadcast transmits a control-direction ASDU with send/no reply to link address 255 (clause 6.2.3), between two exchanges of the link, also while the equipment sets DFC (clause 6.3). Nothing is confirmed. It returns [iec103.ErrLinkDown](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-iec60870-5/iec103#ErrLinkDown) when the link goes down before the link loop took it.

#### func (Client) BroadcastClockSync

```go
func (c *Client) BroadcastClockSync(t time.Time) error
```

BroadcastClockSync sends ASDU 6 with the global common address to link address 255 (send/no reply, clause 7.4.2), with t advanced by the time it waited for the link like [Client.ClockSync](#func-client-clocksync). Equipment that answers a broadcast synchronization with ASDU 6 delivers it to the Handler.

#### func (Client) ClockSync

```go
func (c *Client) ClockSync(ctx context.Context, t time.Time) (cp.Timestamp, error)
```

ClockSync synchronizes the clock of the protection equipment with an addressed ASDU 6 (send/confirm, clause 7.4.2) and returns the time of the ASDU 6 it answers with: the time of the command, corrected by the equipment for transmission and processing. The command carries t advanced by the time it waited for the link, the time of its transmission.

```go
func (c *Client) Close() error
```

#### func (Client) Command

```go
func (c *Client) Command(ctx context.Context, fun iec103.FunctionType, inf iec103.InfoNumber, dco iec103.DPI) error
```

Command sends a general command (ASDU 20, clause 7.4.4) and waits for its acknowledgement: ASDU 1 with the same FUN and INF, cause 20 or 21 and the command's RII as SIN. A negative acknowledgement returns an error wrapping [iec103.ErrNegative](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-iec60870-5/iec103#ErrNegative). The change of state the command causes follows with cause 12 and reaches the Handler. Clause 7.4.4 allows one command procedure at a time: a second concurrent call returns [iec103.ErrBusy](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-iec60870-5/iec103#ErrBusy). A command that [iec103.CommandAllowed](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-iec60870-5/iec103#CommandAllowed) refuses (DCO 0 or 3, OFF where table 17 defines only ON, or an INF outside table 17 with a compatible function type) returns [iec103.ErrInvalid](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-iec60870-5/iec103#ErrInvalid).

#### func (Client) Disturbance

```go
func (c *Client) Disturbance(ctx context.Context, fun iec103.FunctionType, fan uint16) (*iec103.Disturbance, error)
```

Disturbance transfers the recorded disturbance fan of function type fun with the procedure of clause 7.4.7 (figure 10):

 1. ASDU 24 "selection of fault", answered by ASDU 26;
 2. ASDU 24 "request for disturbance data", answered by ASDU 28;
 3. ASDU 24 "request for tags", answered by ASDUs 29 and an ASDU 31, acknowledged by ASDU 25 "tags transmitted successfully", or "not successfully" when the equipment aborted them (TOO 40) or the initial states were not at position 0 (clause 7.4.7);
 4. for each ASDU 27 the equipment offers: ASDU 24 "channel request", answered by ASDUs 30 and an ASDU 31, acknowledged by ASDU 25 positive when NFE runs without gaps up to NOE, negative otherwise or when the equipment aborted the channel (TOO 37);
 5. the ASDU 31 "end of disturbance data", acknowledged by ASDU 25: negative when tags or a channel were, or when fewer channels came than NOC announced.

A negative acknowledgement returns the record with an error wrapping [iec103.ErrNegative](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-iec60870-5/iec103#ErrNegative); clause 7.4.7 lets the equipment then offer the transfer again. An abortion of the whole transfer by the equipment (TOO 34) is acknowledged negatively and returns [iec103.ErrAborted](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-iec60870-5/iec103#ErrAborted). The ctx should allow for the whole transfer; on its expiry the transfer is left as it is (no abortion order is sent). One transfer at a time.

#### func (Client) DisturbanceList

```go
func (c *Client) DisturbanceList(ctx context.Context, fun iec103.FunctionType) ([]iec103.RecordedFault, error)
```

DisturbanceList requests the list of recorded disturbances of function type fun (ASDU 24 with TOO 24, clause 7.2.6.26) and returns the faults of the ASDU 23 the equipment answers with. The equipment also sends ASDU 23 on its own (a new disturbance, after a transfer, after a general interrogation, clause 7.4.7); those reach the Handler.

#### func (Client) GenericInterrogation

```go
func (c *Client) GenericInterrogation(ctx context.Context) ([]iec103.DataSet, error)
```

GenericInterrogation runs the general interrogation of generic data (clause 7.4.8.7): ASDU 21 with INF 245 and cause 9, then collects the data sets of the ASDUs 10 with INF 244, cause 9 and the same RII until the end (ASDU 10, INF 245, cause 10). Spontaneous generic data in between reaches the Handler only.

#### func (Client) GenericRead

```go
func (c *Client) GenericRead(ctx context.Context, inf iec103.InfoNumber, items ...iec103.Item) (*GenericResult, error)
```

GenericRead sends a generic read command (ASDU 21, cause 42) with information number inf (240, 241, 243 or 244, table 18) and the given generic identifiers, and collects the answers (ASDU 10, or ASDU 11 for 243) with the same RII until CONT = 0 (clauses 7.4.8.5 and 7.4.8.6). An answer with cause 43 is not an error: Cause reports it and the data sets carry the generic reply codes. Clause 7.4.8.4 allows one generic read at a time: a second concurrent call returns [iec103.ErrBusy](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-iec60870-5/iec103#ErrBusy).

#### func (Client) GenericWrite

```go
func (c *Client) GenericWrite(ctx context.Context, inf iec103.InfoNumber, sets ...iec103.DataSet) (*GenericResult, error)
```

GenericWrite sends a generic write command (ASDU 10, cause 40, clause 7.4.8.6.3) with information number inf and the data sets, split over several ASDUs with the same RII and COUNT toggling when they need it:

  - 248 (write entry) has no application answer; it returns nil, nil once the link layer confirmed the last ASDU;
  - 249 (write with confirmation) waits for the echo with cause 44;
  - 250 (write with execution) waits for cause 40 or 41;
  - 251 (write abort) waits for cause 40.

For 250 and 251 every ASDU but the last carries INF 248 and CONT = 1, and the last INF 250 or 251 and CONT = 0 (figure 17); [Client.BeginWrite](#func-client-beginwrite) builds such a write over several calls. Cause 41 returns the answer with an error wrapping [iec103.ErrNegative](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-iec60870-5/iec103#ErrNegative); the data sets of the answer carry the generic reply codes. Clause 7.4.8.4 allows one generic write at a time.

#### func (Client) Identification

```go
func (c *Client) Identification() *iec103.ASDU
```

Identification returns the last identification (ASDU 5) the protection equipment sent, after a reset or a start/restart (clause 7.4.1), or nil.

#### func (Client) Interrogate

```go
func (c *Client) Interrogate(ctx context.Context) ([]*iec103.ASDU, error)
```

Interrogate runs a general interrogation (clause 7.4.3): ASDU 7 with a new scan number, then collects the answers with cause 9 until the termination (ASDU 8) with the same scan number. Time-tagged messages whose SIN is not the scan number are left out: clause 7.4.3 has the control system discard GI answers of an earlier cycle. Generic data (ASDU 10, the general interrogation of generic data) is not part of it.

#### func (Client) Send

```go
func (c *Client) Send(ctx context.Context, a *iec103.ASDU) error
```

Send transmits a control-direction ASDU with send/confirm and returns when the link layer confirmed it, or at the deadline of ctx: the link layer then still finishes the exchange, repeating the frame until it is answered or Link.Retries ran out. Answers reach the Handler.

### type Config

```go
type Config struct {
	// Link holds the link timing. The address field is always one octet
	// (clause 6.2.3); Link.FT12 is set accordingly.
	Link link.Config

	// LinkAddr is the link address of the protection equipment, 0..254.
	LinkAddr uint8
	// CommonAddr is the common address of ASDU of the protection
	// equipment. Zero means LinkAddr, which clause 7.2.4 makes the normal
	// case and the system functions require.
	CommonAddr uint8

	// ResetFCB initializes the link with reset FCB (function 7) instead of
	// reset CU (function 0); clause 7.4.1 leaves the choice to the control
	// system. Reset CU also clears the transmit buffer of the equipment.
	ResetFCB bool
	// NoInitTimeSync and NoInitGI leave out the time synchronization and
	// the general interrogation that follow the initialization (clause
	// 7.4.1, figure 3; clause 7.4.3).
	NoInitTimeSync bool
	NoInitGI       bool

	// PollInterval is the pause between class 2 polls when the equipment
	// has nothing to send. Zero means [DefaultPollInterval].
	PollInterval time.Duration
	// RequestTimeout bounds every request whose context has no deadline.
	// Zero means [DefaultRequestTimeout]. A disturbance data transfer
	// usually needs a longer context.
	RequestTimeout time.Duration
	// RetryInterval is the pause before the link is initialized again
	// after a failure. Zero means [DefaultRetryInterval].
	RetryInterval time.Duration

	// Location is the time zone of the time tags; nil means UTC.
	Location *time.Location

	// Handler receives every monitor-direction ASDU, the answers to
	// requests included (they are also returned by the request). It runs
	// on a goroutine of its own, in order; it may issue requests.
	Handler func(a *iec103.ASDU)
	// OnState is called with each change of the link state.
	OnState func(s iec103.State, err error)
	// Logger receives the log entries; nil is silent.
	Logger iec60870.Logger
}
```

Config configures a client.

### type GenericResult

```go
type GenericResult struct {
	// Cause is 42 (valid data) unless an answer had cause 43 (invalid
	// data, the sets then carry generic reply codes), or the cause of a
	// write answer (40, 41 or 44).
	Cause    iec103.Cause
	Sets     []iec103.DataSet
	GIN      iec103.GIN
	Elements []iec103.DescElement
	// ASDUs are the answers as received.
	ASDUs []*iec103.ASDU
}
```

GenericResult is the answer to a generic service (clause 7.4.8): the data sets of every ASDU 10, or the GIN and description elements of every ASDU 11, with the same RII, in order.

### type StagedWrite

```go
type StagedWrite struct {

	// COUNT of the next ASDU
	// INF of every ASDU but the last: 248, or 249 for GenericWrite

}
```

StagedWrite is a generic write built over several calls (clause 7.4.8.6.3, figure 17): ASDUs 10 with INF 248 (write entry) and CONT = 1, then a last ASDU with INF 250 (write with execution) or 251 (write abort) and CONT = 0, all with one RII and COUNT toggling from ASDU to ASDU. It holds the client's one generic write (clause 7.4.8.4) until [StagedWrite.Execute](#func-stagedwrite-execute) or [StagedWrite.Abort](#func-stagedwrite-abort); a StagedWrite is not safe for concurrent use.

#### func (StagedWrite) Abort

```go
func (w *StagedWrite) Abort(ctx context.Context) (*GenericResult, error)
```

Abort sends INF 251 (write abort) with CONT = 0: the equipment drops the staged data without activating it. It waits for the answer, cause 40.

#### func (StagedWrite) Execute

```go
func (w *StagedWrite) Execute(ctx context.Context, sets ...iec103.DataSet) (*GenericResult, error)
```

Execute sends the last ASDU with INF 250 (write with execution) and CONT = 0, carrying sets (more ASDUs with INF 248 before it when they need them), and waits for the answer: cause 40, or 41 with an error wrapping [iec103.ErrNegative](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-iec60870-5/iec103#ErrNegative) and the generic reply codes in the answer.

#### func (StagedWrite) RII

```go
func (w *StagedWrite) RII() uint8
```

RII returns the return information identifier of the write.

#### func (StagedWrite) Stage

```go
func (w *StagedWrite) Stage(ctx context.Context, sets ...iec103.DataSet) error
```

Stage sends sets with INF 248 and CONT = 1, in as many ASDUs as they need. Nothing is answered; the equipment keeps the data until the write is executed or aborted.
